name: brokerage-reads
description: Selection among the read tools. Every scenario here is a thing a customer actually says, and the expectation is a statement about the trace rather than about the wording of the reply. The forbidTools lists are the half that earns its keep: it is easy to get an agent to call the right tool and hard to stop it calling three more.

scenarios.utterance: What accounts do I have with you?
scenarios.why: The simplest possible first turn. One call, no guessing.

scenarios.utterance: How much can I spend in my everyday brokerage account?
scenarios.why: Buying power, not cash, and not a preview. The nickname has to be resolved to an identifier first, which is the producer graph doing its job.

scenarios.utterance: What am I holding in the everyday brokerage account?
scenarios.why: Positions, not tax lots. An agent that reaches for lots here is spending a call and a paragraph on something nobody asked about.

scenarios.utterance: What are Apple, Microsoft and Nvidia trading at right now?
scenarios.why: One batched call, not three. This is the scenario that catches a singular quote tool.

scenarios.utterance: How has Nvidia done over the last month?
scenarios.why: Price history, not a quote. Both are plausible and only one answers the question.

scenarios.utterance: Do I have anything still working?
scenarios.why: The default state filter is WORKING, so a correct call passes no state at all.

scenarios.utterance: What price did I actually get on that Nvidia buy?
scenarios.why: Executions, not the order's average. The fills are the answer to 'what did I pay'.

scenarios.utterance: If I sell some of my Apple, which shares would go first and what would the tax look like?
scenarios.why: Tax lots, and no order anywhere. A question about a sale is not an instruction to sell.
AAPL and APLE both match. A search is the right first move, and the reply should name the alternatives rather than assume.

scenarios.utterance: Am I too concentrated in any one stock in the everyday brokerage account?
scenarios.why: The weight is already in the positions payload, so this needs no arithmetic and no second tool.
